subject: Proposal: phased milestone shift and acceptance window
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Susa Shah <susa.shah@acme.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: phased milestone shift and acceptance window

Susa / team,

Quick note following the workshop this week — the acceptance gating for your next integration milestone is tighter than expected given the current test matrix and the latency profile we saw on your privacy-heavy dataset. To avoid a hard miss on the contract close date, we propose a phased milestone shift:

- Phase 1 (Week 0–2): Ship the data ingestion + baseline evals.
- Phase 2 (Week 2–4): Run the full suite (privacy-preserving evals) with extended KV cache tuning.
- Phase 3 (Week 4–6): Final acceptance, performance validation, and go/no-go review.

This gives a formal 2-week buffer on the final acceptance window while still delivering usable artifacts early. Attached: draft MAP and updated eval plan.

Questions: are there any procurement constraints on a phased acceptance? If not, would Acme accept a proposed target close moved from Apr 30 -> May 14 with a 50% partial acceptance milestone on Apr 30?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments (2): 2027-03-20_MAP_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval-plan_v2.docx (docx)

From: Susa Shah <susa.shah@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased milestone shift and acceptance window

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear plan. Procurement flagged two items: (1) any date shift needs written approval from our legal team and (2) we need a firm SLA for the final performance targets if we agree to an extension. Can you provide a short addendum that defines the partial-acceptance deliverables and the pass/fail criteria for the final run?

Also: we have a board quarterly close on May 6. Shifting final acceptance to May 14 is tough from a financial close perspective. Could the partial acceptance on Apr 30 be expanded (i.e., more gating satisfied) so our finance team can treat Apr 30 as a recognized milestone for revenue recognition?

Susa
Susa Shah
Director, Platform Integrations — Acme Corp
susa.shah@acme.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: phased milestone shift and acceptance window

Thanks for the thread — looping in pricing and CS notes. Per procurement ask, I drafted a concise addendum that spells out:

- Partial Acceptance (Apr 30): data ingestion complete, baseline evals pass with 95% of targeted P95 latency, and documented runbook for privacy mode.
- Final Acceptance (May 14): full eval suite pass (quality metrics within 2% of baseline) and SLA: 99.5% availability for the production test harness over a 7-day run.

Marissa — can you confirm whether we can tighten the Apr 30 partial acceptance criteria to cover revenue recognition (i.e., include one production-like scenario validated end-to-end)? If not, we should offer a commercial concession (one month of discounted committed capacity) to bridge the finance ask.

Rishi — if we need to compress Phase 2 into 1 week, what incremental engineering hours do we need? Please add to the MAP spreadsheet.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: addendum_partial_acceptance.docx (draft)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Susa Shah <susa.shah@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: phased milestone shift and acceptance window — next steps and executive ask

Susa — quick follow-up with an offer to keep Acme on the current financial close cadence: we can do either

A) Tighten Apr 30 partial acceptance so it includes one production-like E2E scenario validated end-to-end (additional engineering sprint of ~24 hours). No change to final acceptance date (May 14), but finance can treat Apr 30 as a recognized milestone. Commercial: no discount; we absorb sprint cost.

or

B) Keep the looser Apr 30 partial acceptance, move final acceptance to May 14, and apply a commercial concession: 25% off committed capacity for one month to offset the close slip.

If you can confirm preference by end of day Fri Mar 26, we will: (1) update the MAP spreadsheet and addendum, (2) request legal to sign the short addendum, and (3) schedule a 30-min alignment call with engineering to lock sprint dates.

If procurement needs written confirmation of the SLA pass/fail criteria we included the addendum link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MAP-eval

Thanks — Jordan
